reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: Later-onset, less severe form of lysosomal acid lipase (LIPA) deficiency, contrasting with the fulminant infantile Wolman phenotype
Presents in childhood or adulthood with hepatomegaly, elevated transaminases and progressive hepatic steatosis that can advance to fibrosis and cirrhosis
Characteristic dyslipidaemia is a mixed pattern with high LDL cholesterol and low HDL cholesterol, mimicking familial hypercholesterolaemia and driving premature atherosclerosis
Microvesicular and macrovesicular steatosis on liver biopsy can be misread as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
A common LIPA splice variant (exon 8 skipping) accounts for many late-onset cases
Diagnosis is confirmed by low lysosomal acid lipase enzyme activity and LIPA genetic testing
Enzyme replacement therapy with recombinant lysosomal acid lipase (sebelipase alfa) is available, alongside lipid-lowering therapy and monitoring of liver disease
reference.pathophysiology: Lysosomal acid lipase hydrolyses cholesteryl esters and triglycerides delivered to the lysosome via receptor-mediated lipoprotein uptake. Partial deficiency in cholesteryl ester storage disease leads to lysosomal accumulation of cholesteryl esters and triglycerides, predominantly in hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, intestinal mucosa and the arterial wall. Reduced release of free cholesterol from the lysosome disturbs cellular cholesterol homeostasis, upregulating endogenous cholesterol synthesis and LDL receptor pathways, which produces the atherogenic dyslipidaemia; progressive hepatic lipid storage causes steatosis, fibrosis and, over time, cirrhosis.
additionalDifferentials: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and steatohepatitis
Familial hypercholesterolaemia and other primary dyslipidaemias
Niemann-Pick disease type C and other lipid storage disorders
additionalInvestigations: Lysosomal acid lipase enzyme activity assay (dried blood spot or leucocytes)
LIPA molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Fasting lipid profile showing high LDL and low HDL cholesterol
Liver function tests and liver imaging for steatosis and fibrosis
Liver biopsy demonstrating lipid-laden hepatocytes and characteristic storage
Cardiovascular risk assessment for premature atherosclerosis
redFlags: Progression to hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis or portal hypertension
Premature cardiovascular disease from severe dyslipidaemia
Rapidly rising transaminases or worsening hepatic function
Splenomegaly with cytopenias indicating advanced liver disease
reference.prognosis: The course is variable and slower than Wolman disease, but untreated disease can progress to cirrhosis and accelerated atherosclerosis; enzyme replacement therapy and lipid-lowering treatment can improve hepatic and lipid parameters and alter the natural history.
pitfalls: Labelling the liver disease as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and missing the enzyme defect
Attributing the dyslipidaemia solely to familial hypercholesterolaemia
Failing to test lysosomal acid lipase activity in unexplained hepatomegaly with dyslipidaemia
Underestimating cardiovascular risk in an apparently mild hepatic presentation
references: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
